summary: Document automatic destination URL normalization for link creation.
rationale: Users and operators need to know which URL components change, how the existing create API reports the normalized destination, and that the behavior requires no configuration and does not rewrite existing links.
content:
# Destination URL normalization

When you create a short link, the service normalizes its destination before saving it. The normalized URL is returned by the create endpoint, shown in link details, and used for redirects.

Normalization lowercases the URL scheme and host, removes the default port (`:80` for HTTP and `:443` for HTTPS), and removes query parameters whose names start with `utm_` (case-insensitively). Other query parameters and the fragment are retained. If all query parameters are removed, the URL has no query string.

## API usage

Create links using the existing endpoint and request shape:

```http
POST /api/v1/links
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "longUrl": "HTTPS://Example.COM:443/docs?utm_source=newsletter&ref=home&utm_campaign=spring#overview"
}
```

A successful request returns `201 Created`. The `longUrl` in the response is normalized:

```http
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Location: /api/v1/links/Abc1234
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "code": "Abc1234",
  "shortUrl": "https://short.example/Abc1234",
  "longUrl": "https://example.com/docs?ref=home#overview",
  "createdAtUtc": "2026-10-20T12:00:00Z",
  "expiresAtUtc": null
}
```

The code, short URL, and timestamp values above are illustrative. No request or response fields have been added. `GET /api/v1/links/{code}` reports the saved normalized destination, and following the short URL redirects to that destination.

## Configuration

No configuration is required. Normalization runs automatically for newly created links. There is no setting to disable or customize the normalization rules. Existing settings that configure the public short-link base URL affect `shortUrl`, not destination normalization.

## Limitations and behavior

- Only default HTTP and HTTPS ports are removed. Non-default ports are retained.
- Only query parameters whose names begin with `utm_`, regardless of the casing of that prefix, are removed. Other parameters are preserved; their order is not a normalization target.
- URL fragments are preserved.
- Previously saved links are not rewritten. Normalization applies when a link is created.
- Idempotency continues to compare the original request body. Requests with different original URLs can therefore conflict when reused with the same idempotency key, even if those URLs normalize to the same destination.
- Normalization does not change URL validation, expiry handling, or link creation limits.
